articles.title: Parish and Park Groups Team Up on Basketball Court
articles.deck: The money will be spent over the next year, with the first work starting in September.

articles.title: Letter: Support the Saturday Cleanup Day
body: To the editor: I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the January meeting. Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed.

Please keep the Saturday cleanup day in the budget. Many of us on Rail Court use it every week. To the editor: I have lived on Rail Court for 40 years, and I want to say what a difference St. Brendan’s Parish has made.
I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the January meeting. Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed.
Lydia Yates, Hickory Ridge

articles.title: Canal Park Garden Club Adds After-school Reading Program
articles.deck: The work is expected to take 6 weeks and will be paid for with $850 raised locally.
body: The group has raised $850 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food.

Lamar Brennan, who has lived on Bramble Terrace for 6 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected. The Canal Park Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.

The effort began in January when a handful of neighbors met at the Hickory Ridge rec center to talk about after-school reading program. Anyone interested can attend the next planning meeting at the Hickory Ridge rec center on Thursday at 7 p.m.

articles.title: Felix Fontaine, 67, Longtime Volunteer
articles.deck: Friends remember Felix Fontaine for the many years of service to Hickory Ridge.
body: Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Foundry Row Mutual Aid Group in his or her name.
Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Hickory Ridge. Felix Fontaine died in June at home on Rail Court, at the age of 67.

articles.title: Council Delays Vote on Kiln Place Community Garden
articles.deck: The vote came after 32 residents spoke at Tuesday’s session.
body: The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first. Residents of Upper Commons said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street.
Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days. Public works estimates the work will take about 32 weeks once it starts in October.
Councilmember Gwen Fontaine asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $12,000.

body: Students will meet on Thursday afternoons in the Eastgate community hall, and transportation will be provided for those who need it. Principal Vincent Bruckner said the program was built with help from parents and local volunteers.

articles.title: Letter: The Park Bench Program on Wren Lane Needs Attention
body: To the editor: I have lived on Wren Lane for 25 years, and I want to say what a difference the Stonebridge Trail Crew has made. Please keep the park bench program in the budget. Many of us on Wren Lane use it every week.
I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the July meeting. Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed.
